I'm scanning the grid row by row to locate all the 2x2 blocks made entirely of zeros, planning to handle overlapping blocks according to the algorithm's rules.

Continuing to scan the grid rows, I've now got the full data laid out and am starting to search for 2x2 blocks of all zeros by checking column pairs across adjacent rows.

Continuing to scan adjacent rows for matching zero-pairs across columns, I find another match at (4,11), then keep checking remaining column pairs through rows 5 through 9 without finding further matches yet.

Continuing to scan rows 9 through 14 for matching zero-pairs across adjacent columns, I finally find a valid match at (13,15) where consecutive rows both have zeros lining up in columns 15-16.

Moving further down, I check rows 15 through 17 and find another valid pair at (16,2), while ruling out several other candidates due to mismatched values. Then I start validating overlapping candidates like (3,11) and (4,11) by checking their neighboring columns to confirm they're not blocked from being painted.

Both pass the check, so they merge into a single region spanning rows 3-5, columns 11-12. I now compile the full list of red cells: (0,0)-(1,1), (1,8)-(2,9), (3,11)-(5,12), (13,15)-(14,16), and (16,2)-(17,3), then move to constructing the final output grid.

I'm scanning the grid for 2x2 blocks where all four cells are zero, checking row1-row2 at columns 6-7 and row2-row3 at columns 7-8 as candidates.

Since both pass the hollow check (neighboring cells aren't both zero on either side), both get painted, covering cells (1,6),(1,7),(2,6),(2,7),(2,8),(3,7),(3,8).

Continuing the scan, I find another candidate block at rows5-6, columns 11-12, and I'm checking its left/right neighbors to confirm it should be painted too.

Now I'm checking a similar block at rows5-6, columns14-15, verifying its neighbors don't both contain zeros, then moving on to examine rows12-13 near columns 1-6 for more zero blocks to paint.

Testing (12,3) and (12,4) for overlap: since both share overlapping neighbors, I skip pass1 for these, but pass2 (checking vertically) shows no red above or below (12,3), so I paint it — which then disqualifies (12,4) as hollow since it now touches red.

But I realize both were actually computed in the same batch before painting occurred, so both (12,3) and (12,4) end up passing and get painted red across rows 12-13, columns 3, 4, and 5. I continue scanning other row pairs for similar hollow patterns but find none matching in rows 0-1, 6-7, or 8-9.

Then checking rows 16-17 columns 5-6, I find another matching block with red 5s on both left and right neighbors, so I paint those too. Scanning further through rows 2-3, 8-9, and 4-6 for other candidate blocks, I don't find any more matches.
